# orly?

> A completion gate for agentic loops. An LLM turns your goal into specifiers; a System
> One model (TypeSafe's Jev) checks them all in one request at the end of every turn and
> returns what isn't true; the agent goes back to work until they hold. A library and a
> CLI, with one small adapter per host.

Read these in whatever order the question demands. Each is self-contained.

## Docs

- [Why the end of a turn](docs/why.txt): where to attach a gate and why nowhere else works, the two question layers, what the Choice is for, how the loop terminates.
- [Installing](docs/install.txt): setup, how the API key is supplied without putting a secret in a config file, where `.orly` lives, every environment variable.
- [Writing specs](docs/specs.txt): the four rules for a spec that can actually be judged, why conditional specs need an explicit branch, and how to stop the agent being the only source of evidence about itself.
- [Measured](docs/measured.txt): the current fixture table and per-hazard separations, regenerated by `bun test/calibrate.ts --write` rather than hand-typed.
- [Calibration](docs/calibration.txt): measured fixture tables, how the cuts were fitted, why a single global spec threshold cannot work, and why the Score primitive is the wrong tool for "is it done".
- [The state is the hard part](docs/state.txt): ten wrong numbers, none of them the model's fault — the flush race, the preamble, discarded mid-turn declarations, failures scrolling out of the window.
- [The agent edits its own examiner](docs/guard.txt): what counts as weakening the gate, the two enforcement points, and the limit of what can be enforced from inside the session.
- [Getting better](docs/learning.txt): hot reload, the verdict log, free labels, `orly fit`, and how one fitted wording reaches every project.
- [Any agentic loop](docs/porting.txt): the module layout, the CLI contract, the Turn shape, and how to write an adapter.
